regulations.title: Register a trade name if selling under a name other than your own
regulations.summary: If you sell cosmetics under a brand or business name that isn't simply your own legal name, Alberta requires you to file a trade name (or partnership) registration with the Corporate Registry before operating under that name.
regulations.regulation_name: Partnership Act / Business Corporations Act - trade name registration
regulations.authority: Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction - Corporate Registry
regulations.action_required: File a Declaration of Trade Name (sole proprietorship) or Declaration of Partnership through an Alberta registry agent before selling under your brand name.
regulations.penalty_note: Operating under an unregistered trade name doesn't secure naming rights and can create compliance gaps if the name is challenged.
regulations.source_name: Government of Alberta - Register a business name

regulations.title: Extra-provincial corporation registration within 30 days of doing business in Alberta
regulations.summary: If your cosmetics company is already incorporated in another province or country and you start doing business in Alberta, you must register it as an extra-provincial corporation within 30 days of beginning operations here.
regulations.regulation_name: Business Corporations Act, Part 21 - extra-provincial registration
regulations.authority: Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction - Corporate Registry
regulations.action_required: Reserve your corporate name for use in Alberta, then file a Statement of Registration (Form 33) with supporting incorporation documents within 30 days of carrying on business in Alberta.
regulations.penalty_note: Carrying on business in Alberta without the required extra-provincial registration is a violation of the Business Corporations Act.
regulations.source_name: Government of Alberta - Register an out-of-province corporation

regulations.title: Direct seller's licence for door-to-door or home-party cosmetic sales
regulations.summary: If you sell cosmetics through door-to-door visits, home parties, or similar direct-sales models (common for beauty brands), Alberta requires the business to hold a direct seller's licence and post financial security, on top of any other business registration.
regulations.regulation_name: Consumer Protection Act and Direct Selling Business Licensing Regulation
regulations.authority: Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction
regulations.action_required: Apply for a direct seller's licence and post the required financial security with Service Alberta before conducting door-to-door or home-party cosmetic sales.
regulations.penalty_note: Conducting licensable direct sales activity without a direct seller's licence is an offence under the Consumer Protection Act.
regulations.source_name: Government of Alberta - Direct seller's licence

regulations.title: No false or misleading claims on cosmetic labels or advertising
regulations.summary: Alberta's Consumer Protection Act prohibits false, misleading, or deceptive statements about your cosmetics' benefits, ingredients, or origin in labelling and advertising - a separate provincial layer on top of federal cosmetic labelling rules.
regulations.regulation_name: Consumer Protection Act, RSA 2000, c C-26.3
regulations.authority: Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction - Consumer Investigations Unit
regulations.action_required: Review product claims and packaging copy for accuracy before marketing in Alberta, and avoid unverifiable or misleading claims about ingredients or effects.
regulations.penalty_note: Violations can lead to consumer complaints, investigation by the Consumer Investigations Unit, and enforcement action under the Consumer Protection Act.
